newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE officials consider Albanian options.
newsitem.headline: OSCE officials consider Albanian options.

text.p: Officials from Europe's main security organisation discussed on Wednesday what action the body should take if talks between Albania's bickering political parties broke down completely.

Franz Vranitzky, envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, had given the nation's politicians until midnight on Tuesday to reach a compromise on the format of elections planned for June 29.
But as the deadline ticked past Prime Minister Bashkim Fino was still trying to bridge the political impasse.
"Discussions are going on among the parties in Tirana and within the OSCE secretariat in Vienna. Officials are gauging what sort of measures can be taken," an OSCE spokesman said.
Vranitzky is due to address the Vienna-based OSCE's permanent council at 0800 GMT on Thursday.

A diplomatic source warned that the international community was running out of patience with Albania, which has been afflicted by near-anarchy since January when the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes caused national uproar.
"It is time for Albanian politicians to come up with a solution to the gridlock," the source said.
Vranitzky has travelled to Tirana several times to try to smooth the differences between Berisha's rightist Democrats, who dominate parliament, and opposition parties, led by the Socialists.
OSCE officials say it and other international organisations may withdraw aid if Albanian politicians fail to reach a pact.
